feedback.problem: Use the method of Lagrange multipliers to find the maximum value of the function $f(x,y,z)=2x+y+5z$ on the ellipsoid $9{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+9{z}^{2}=38.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We need to find the maximum value of $f$ subject to the constraint $g(x,y,z)=9{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+9{z}^{2}=38.$ 

Since $f(x,y,z)$ is continuous and the constraint is closed and bounded, $f(x,y,z)$ reaches a global maximum and a global minimum on the constraint. 

Therefore, by the method of Lagrange multipliers, we must solve the following system:

$$
∇f(x,y,z)=\lambda ∇g(x,y,z),\,g(x,y,z)=38
$$

We start by solving the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\lambda ∇g(x,y,z) \\ ⟨{f}_{x}(x,y,z),{f}_{y}(x,y,z),{f}_{z}(x,y,z)⟩ & =\lambda ⟨{g}_{x}(x,y,z),{g}_{y}(x,y,z),{g}_{z}(x,y,z)⟩ \\ ⟨2,1,5⟩ & =\lambda ⟨18x,2y,18z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we cannot have $\lambda =0$ since this leads to a contradiction in the above equation. Therefore, assuming $\lambda \ne 0,$ we have the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2=18\lambda x \\ 1=2\lambda y \\ 5=18\lambda z\end{aligned}\,⇒\,{\begin{aligned}x=\frac{1}{9\lambda } \\ y=\frac{1}{2\lambda } \\ z=\frac{5}{18\lambda }\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute our expressions for $x,\,y$ and $z$ into the condition $g(x,y,z)=38$ and solve for $\lambda ,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+9{z}^{2} & =38 \\ 9(\frac{1}{81{\lambda }^{2}})+\frac{1}{4{\lambda }^{2}}+9(\frac{25}{324{\lambda }^{2}}) & =38 \\ \frac{1}{9{\lambda }^{2}}+\frac{1}{4{\lambda }^{2}}+\frac{25}{36{\lambda }^{2}} & =38 \\ \frac{19}{18{\lambda }^{2}} & =38 \\ {\lambda }^{2} & =\frac{1}{36} \\ \lambda  & =\pm \frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find $x,\,y$ and $z.$ This gives

$$
x=\pm \frac{2}{3},\,y=\pm 3,\,z=\pm \frac{5}{3}.
$$

Therefore, $f$ has possible extreme values at the points 

$$
(\frac{2}{3},3,\frac{5}{3}),\,(-\frac{2}{3},-3,-\frac{5}{3}).
$$

We evaluate $f$ at each of these points. These are given in the following table:

| $\,(x,y,z)\,$ | $\,(-\frac{2}{3},-3,-\frac{5}{3})\,$ | $\,(\frac{2}{3},3,\frac{5}{3})\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\,f(x,y,z)\,$ | $\,-\frac{38}{3}\,$ | $\,\frac{38}{3}\,$ |

$$

$$

Therefore, the function reaches a maximum value at $(\frac{2}{3},3,\frac{5}{3}),$ and its maximum value is $\frac{38}{3}.$
